- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. ### ① Derived judgments

**Gate verdicts on the head.** At 2026-10-20T22:01Z, 40 check-run names: every one success or skipped except `Test Core (3/6)`, in_progress. Re-read at 2026-10-20T22:14Z: 41 names, all success or skipped, `Test Core (3/6)` included. `Check Changeset`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Lint & Repo Gates` (carries `check:i18n`), `Type Check · workspace`, `Build Core`, `Test Core (1..6)`, the card-claims-branch and single-writer checks: success.

**The refusal's reach — who is refused now who answered before.** Every delete of a `sys_business_unit` row that enters `engine.delete` with `where.id` runs `cascadeDeleteRelations`, whose walk resolves `parent_business_unit_id` through `cascadeRelationBehavior` as `fdef.deleteBehavior || 'set_null'`, now `restrict`, and refuses when any row outside the cascade set still holds the id. Before this head the same walk wrote `null` into each child (the spec materializes `set_null` when the key is undefined, field.zod.ts:2981). Write shapes that reach that branch:
- by id: `DELETE /api/v1/data/sys_business_unit/:id` (crud-routes.ts → `protocol.deleteData` → `engine.delete(object, { where: { id } })`), the SDK's `data.delete`, MCP `delete_record({ objectName, recordId })` (mcp-http-tools.ts) and the data-action undo of a create (`undoDeleteRequest`, data-action-routes.ts) are one door. Refused while a child exists. Right.
- bulk: `POST …/deleteMany` is `runDeleteManyLoop`, one `engine.delete({ where: { id } })` per id in the caller's order; a refused parent is one `results[]` row carrying `DELETE_RESTRICTED`, the loop stops on it unless `continueOnError` (declared default `false`, batch.zod.ts:81) and the tail is `NOT_ATTEMPTED`; `atomic: true` rolls the batch back. Leaf-to-root completes, root-first refuses the root. Right.
- `/batch` (`batchData`, `case 'delete'`): the same per-id `engine.delete`, the same stop semantics. Right.
- an import: `import-runner.ts` deletes nothing. Not a shape of the refusal.
- the console's bulk delete (objectui `main`): not an ordered `deleteMany`, as acceptance note 1 says. `ObjectView.onBulkDelete` calls `actions.deleteRecords`, and `recordDelete.ts` fires one `dataSource.delete(objectName, id)` per selected row in parallel under `Promise.allSettled`, then shows one summary toast (`bulkDeletePartial`, "N deleted, M failed"). A subtree selected whole loses its leaves, keeps its root with a 409, and a second delete of the root succeeds. Nothing is stranded and no batch stops; the refusal's sentence is not shown on that path, only the count (objectui's display, read only). `data-objectstack.bulkDelete` (deleteMany with `continueOnError: true`) exists but is not what ObjectView calls; it would complete the children and refuse the root the same way. The dev's conclusion (loud, retryable) holds; the description of the console path is wrong and corrected here.
- Not reached, unchanged: the engine's predicate branch (a `where` without `id`, `isPredicatePath`) skips the referential pass entirely, as it skipped `set_null` before. No door exposes it for this object (`deleteMany` is ids only, fail-closed) and no caller in the tree predicate-deletes `sys_business_unit`.
- Context: a unit with MEMBERS was already refused on this head's base: `sys_business_unit_member.business_unit_id` is a required lookup with no `deleteBehavior`, which `walkReferencingRelations` escalates to `restrict` (`requiredSetNull && !multiValued`). This PR adds child UNITS to the refusing set; it is the only new refusal.

Platform paths that could meet the refusal, each read in the code:
- an organization's delete: `sys_business_unit.organization_id` is `Field.lookup('sys_organization', { required: false })` with no `deleteBehavior`, so `set_null`: the units stay, parent links untouched; pinned (test 8). Nothing cascades into `sys_business_unit`: its own relations are `parent_business_unit_id` (restrict), `organization_id` and `manager_user_id` (set_null), none `cascade` or `master_detail`, so no cascade set ever holds a unit. Right.
- the v18 ceremony: `organization-ownership-inventory.ts` gives `sys_business_unit` fate `attribution` (anchor `parent_business_unit_id`); neither the inventory nor `organization-ownership.ts` calls a delete. Right.
- the sample-data purge (`marketplace-install-local-purge.ts`): rows are collected per object in the loader's insert order (parents first; within one dataset, record order) and deleted as `[...match.rows].reverse()`, one `engine.delete({ where: { id } })` each; a refused row is counted in `errors`, warned, and the loop continues. The only shipped seed of this object (showcase `orgUnits`: bu_acme, bu_field_ops, bu_west_coast, bu_east_coast, bu_hq_finance, `mode: 'upsert'`) is parent-first, so the purge deletes leaf to root and completes. Right.
- seeds, `os` commands, plugin-sharing: both seed loaders delete nothing; no `sys_business_unit` delete under packages/cli/src; `bu-tree-recompute.ts` binds `afterInsert` / `afterUpdate` / `afterDelete` only (priority 190), and no plugin binds a `beforeDelete` on this object. Right.
- tests and fixtures: the two objectql suites that delete a `sys_business_unit` register their own fixture objects (`name: 'sys_business_unit'`, engine-cascade-federated-tenant-anchor.test.ts:308, engine-delete-restricted-locale.test.ts:30); `bu-tree-recompute.test.ts` drives a fake engine. No existing pin moves; Test Core 1 to 6 green on the head.

**Does any platform-owned path now fail where it completed?** No. Every platform deleter either never addresses a unit or addresses leaves before parents. The claim's stop condition (6300791873: stop and report `needs_decision`) is not met. Right.

**The exemptions.** In-set parent and child: moot for this object, since no cascade reaches it; were one ever to, `walkReferencingRelations` filters `dependents` by `cascadeSetHas(cascadeSet.members, …)` before the `restrict` branch (the #22305 rule), and the by-id delete runs inside one `transaction()` when `planCascadeAtomicity` says `atomic`. Handled as the dev says. A re-parented unit: the probe reads the child's current `parent_business_unit_id`; after the update no row holds the old id, the relation yields zero dependents and the delete proceeds; pinned (test 4). Right.

**The wire answer.** In the restrict branch `required = fdef.deleteBehavior !== 'restrict' && fdef.required === true` is false here, so the key is `delete_restricted` (not `_required`); the en template is `This {{object}} is still referenced by {{count}} {{dependentObject}} record(s) through “{{field}}”. Delete or reassign them first.`, rendered with the labels "Business Unit" and "Parent Business Unit": the sentence the dev quotes, byte for byte, with zh-CN / ja-JP / es-ES siblings in the catalog. `err.status = 409`, `err.code = 'DELETE_RESTRICTED'`, `err.dependentObject = 'sys_business_unit'`, `err.dependentCount` only when `dependentCountIsDisclosable` (the caller's own read of the children yields the same ids). The flat REST door carries `error`, `code`, `dependentObject`, `dependentCount`, `developerMessage` at the top level; the Hono doors put the last three in `error.details`. For the administrator the card describes the count is disclosed and the sentence is true and actionable: the blocking object, how many, and the field to re-point. One nuance the object comment and the changeset elide: a caller who cannot read the children gets the `_opaque` sentence without a count, correct by #12166 and not the administrator addressed. The `developerMessage` ends "…or set deleteBehavior:'cascade' on sys_business_unit.parent_business_unit_id": engine-generic, true of the engine's option space, addressed to a developer editing metadata, and inert here because the object is `managedBy: 'platform'` and the card parked `cascade` rather than ruling it wrong; no user-facing surface renders it (the console toast reads `error`). Not misleading enough to matter; see ③.

**Lost reach vs added access.** Before: the parent delete wrote `null` into each child through the referential clear, and plugin-sharing's `afterUpdate` recompute withdrew `unit_and_subordinates` grants from the detached subtree: a silent loss of reach. After: the refusal is thrown before any row is written, inside the delete's own transaction, so no row changes and no after-hook fires (`beforeDelete` dispatches earlier, and plugin-sharing binds none); the grants anchored above keep reaching the tree. Nothing about the recompute changes: a leaf delete still fires `afterDelete`, a re-parent still fires `afterUpdate`, both still revoke and re-grant. There is no path on which `restrict` leaves a grant stale, because a refused delete changes no membership and no edge; and no access is added, since the post-refusal state is the pre-attempt state. Right.

**The help text and comment.** en (regenerated: the `en.objects.generated.ts` leaf equals the new `description` verbatim), zh-CN, ja-JP and es-ES say the same true thing, that a unit with child units cannot be deleted until they are re-parented or deleted, and nothing false (none promises a count or a code). The object comment is true of the by-id path and names the mechanism (`409 DELETE_RESTRICTED`, this object, the child count; leaf to root completes). The hand edit of the three translated values is the repo's rule: AGENTS.md's translations row says translated-locale VALUES are hand-written and editing one is fine while keys must not move, and each generated file's header says to re-translate a leaf by hand when its source changes; no key moved; the `source-hashes.generated.ts` ledgers carry no entry for `parent_business_unit_id.help`, so the leaf is legacy-trusted and no digest moves. `pnpm check:i18n` runs in `Lint & Repo Gates`, green on the head. Right.

**The pins.** `business-unit-parent-delete-restrict.test.ts` boots a real `ObjectQL` over `SqlDriver` (better-sqlite3 in memory), registers the SHIPPED `SysOrganization` and `SysBusinessUnit` from `@objectstack/platform-objects/identity` (the built declaration, as production reads it), and enters the engine through `engine.delete(object, { where: { id } })`, the exact call `deleteData`, `runDeleteManyLoop` and `batchData` make. Teeth: test 2 asserts code, status, `dependentObject`, `dependentCount` 1 AND the whole tree unchanged; tests 3 to 6 and 8 assert `resolves.toBe(true)` plus the resulting tree. The ablation's red set, judged from the code: with `deleteBehavior: 'restrict'` removed the declaration reads `set_null` (test 1 red), the root delete succeeds and re-roots the child (test 2 red: nothing throws, `err` is not an Error) and test 7 goes red for the same reason; 3, 4, 5, 6 and 8 stay green, since a leaf, a re-parented unit, leaf-to-root loops and an organization delete behave identically under `set_null`. 3 failed / 5 passed, as claimed. One nuance: tests 5 to 7 loop `engine.delete` themselves and do not drive `deleteManyData` or `batchData`, so the `NOT_ATTEMPTED` / `continueOnError` / `atomic` envelope remains the protocol's own pins' claim (unchanged); the test names say "the per-id loop of…", which is honest, and the PR body's wire table measured the real loop.

**The three `open_questions`.**
1. *Bulk order* — **A, keep**, with the facts corrected: the console's bulk delete is N parallel by-id deletes settled together with a summary toast, not an ordered `deleteMany`; a subtree selected whole loses its leaves, keeps its root with a 409, and a retry finishes: refuse-and-retry, never stranded.
